legionPlatformUserData.resolution: Resolve through the native platform user-data convention at install/runtime; do not hardcode source-checkout, plugin-root, project, temporary, or client-cache paths as canonical Legion state.
legionPlatformUserData.rule: This is the only canonical root for Legion-written durable product state.

clientPluginData.rule: Never canonical Legion semantics, migration authority, durable receipt authority, or release truth.

repositoryContextAndEvidence.rule: Legion consumes typed packets only; this root is never copied into, migrated as, or purged by Legion state lifecycle.

durableMemory.rule: Outside Legion state migration, rollback, and purge authority.

projectWorkflowArtifacts.rule: Outside canonical Legion product state. Existing .audit and development workflow artifacts are not migrated or purged as Legion platform state.

rules: Each Legion-written persistent root stores all four fields before it is active.

schema_version identifies the root format; writer_version identifies the runtime that last wrote it; min_reader_version gates compatibility; migration_generation monotonically identifies a committed generation.
Unknown, missing, corrupt, or incompatible metadata fails closed with exact repair guidance; it never defaults to empty success or implicit destructive recreation.
Only one lifecycle mutation holder exists per Legion platform-user-data root.
Lock acquisition validates the canonical root and does not follow a symlink, junction, or reparse point outside the verified Legion-owned boundary.
A failed holder releases no partial active generation; recovery uses the migration journal and snapshot.

runtimeLeases.owner: Active client-owned Legion serve --stdio runtime instances
rules: Each active runtime lease records the release/state compatibility generation it is using and closes at client shutdown/restart/crash recovery.
An incompatible migration waits for all old-generation leases to close; it does not terminate unrelated clients or run a parallel active Legion runtime.
Compatible existing clients may finish under their release-bound generation while a bounded update skew is repaired transactionally.

preconditions: Installed runtime and integration assets pass release-binding verification.
Canonical root ownership and every reparse/link target are verified.
For an incompatible state format change, old runtime leases have closed.
steps: Read and validate current root metadata and compatibility.
Create an immutable pre-upgrade snapshot and migration journal for the current committed generation.
Stage new state and selected integration changes outside the active generation.
Validate staged state, metadata, release binding, and selected client integration health.
Atomically activate the new generation and record its migration_generation.
Retain the prior snapshot until the upgrade/rollback acceptance window closes.
forbidden: In-place destructive mutation without a pre-upgrade snapshot.
Partial activation of runtime, assets, schemas, catalog, tools, integrations, or state.
Source-checkout or plugin-relative fallback for canonical product state.

rollback.trigger: Explicit rollback to a compatible N-1 signed runtime/integration release or failure before new generation activation.
rules: Acquire exclusive state lock and wait for incompatible N leases to close.
Restore the pre-upgrade snapshot atomically with matching N-1 integrations and state metadata.
Verify restored root integrity, release binding, client integration health, and exact rollback outcome before reporting success.
Rollback does not create indefinite dual active runtime execution.
On startup or setup resume, detect an unfinished journal or non-committed generation before exposing tools.
Restore the last verified generation atomically when activation did not commit.
If atomic restoration or snapshot validation cannot be proven, fail closed and direct the user to repair; do not continue with a mixed or guessed state.
Corrupt, incomplete, unreadable, or ownership-invalid state is unavailable, not fresh state.
Repair is explicit, reports the failing root and remediation, preserves unrelated client/project data, and writes a receipt after verification.
Purge is never an automatic corruption recovery action.

acceptance: N reads N-1 only when min_reader_version and the declared migration path permit it.
Migration executes once under exclusive lock from a verified snapshot and atomically activates exactly one N generation.
Old runtime leases close before an incompatible activation; selected integrations bind to N runtime/assets/schemas/catalog/tool contract.
Rollback uses the saved pre-upgrade snapshot and matching N-1 signed release/integrations rather than attempting a lossy reverse transform.
N-1 compatibility is verified before activation and state metadata again names the restored generation.
At no point are N and N-1 active Legion product runtimes against one canonical state root.

uninstallAndPurge.packageManagerUninstall: Removes the machine runtime according to package-manager behavior and does not imply client-integration cleanup or state purge.
uninstallAndPurge.setupRemove: Removes selected Legion integrations transactionally, preserves unrelated configuration, and does not imply runtime uninstall or state purge.

requires: resolved symlink/junction/reparse targets remain inside that root
preview and confirmation of exact deletion targets
post-action receipt containing deleted roots and preserved foreign roots
forbiddenTargets: agent client configuration not owned by Legion

qualificationMatrix: N-1 to N upgrade with an idle root
N-1 to N upgrade while incompatible old runtime lease is active
interruption before activation and during activation
N to N-1 rollback with matching runtime, integration, and snapshot
uninstall then reinstall with retained state
corrupt/incomplete metadata and damaged snapshot handling
two concurrent active clients and active-work update behavior
setup repair, disable, remove, and explicit verified purge
symlink, junction, reparse, stale integration, and release-binding mismatch rejection

developmentOnlyTooling: src/lib/cli/commands/state.mjs snapshot|verify remains a mechanical test-state boundary and is retained as development tooling.
Existing .audit workflow state, decision stores, and review artifacts remain owned by their workflow/project paths rather than becoming native product state.
currentSourceBoundary.implementationStatus: M0 contract only; production native state lifecycle is not implemented by this artifact.
